newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends quiet session barely higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends quiet session barely higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures settled mainly a touch higher in dull dealings Tuesday, buoyed by trade and manufacturer-related buying, floor sources said.
Light speculative selling trimmed gains, they added, confining prices to a narrow range and preventing a test of near-term resistance at $1,349-$1,350 basis the active March contract.
March delivery rose $2 a tonne on the day, to $1,338, after ranging between $1,344 to $1,335. Second-month May firmed $1 to $1,361, while the back months finished up $2 to down $1.
Turnover reached an estimated 6,203 lots, but traders estimated AAs (against actuals) accounted for about 20 percent of the day's volume.
On the charts, traders pegged March's next resistance at $1,359. Support was seen at $1,331, a double bottom on the charts. The next downside target was put near $1,322, March's life-of-contract low.

Ivory Coast exporters said Tuesday Ivorian 1996/97 cocoa arrivals picked up in early January, totalling 640,000-650,000 tonnes by January 13, but still down from the 730,000 tonnes recorded by January 13 last year.

Lagging Ivorian arrivals appeared to confirm views that this year's crop would come in lower than last year's record yield, traders said, although some expected the pace of arrivals to continue to increase in the coming weeks.
In its annual commodity review, brokers GNI forecast Ivory Coast's 1996/97 total output at around 950,000 tonnes, down from 1.20 million last season.

GNI pegged global production at 2.559 million tonnes versus 2.856 million in 1995/96. It said world cocoa supply could post a deficit of 180,000 tonnes in 1996/97 compared with an estimated surplus of 161,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
